subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Octavia Butler was an American science fiction writer known for her novels and short stories.
• She published the novel Kindred in 1979.
• A central character in the novel is a Black woman living in 1970s California.
• Another central character is her white ancestor living as a slaveholder in antebellum Maryland.
prompt: The student wants to introduce the novel Kindred to an audience already familiar with Octavia Butler. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Octavia Butler's settings include both 1970s California and antebellum Maryland.
choices.B: In addition to her novel Kindred, which was published in 1979, American science fiction writer Octavia Butler wrote other novels and short stories.
choices.C: Kindred was not the only novel written by American science fiction writer Octavia Butler.
choices.D: Octavia Butler's novel Kindred centers around two characters, a Black woman in 1970s California and her white ancestor living as a slaveholder in antebellum Maryland.

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer. The sentence effectively introduces Kindred to an audience already familiar with Butler, explaining that the novel centers around two characters and mentioning the author without providing any other identifying information.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. The sentence provides introductory information about Butler; it doesn't effectively introduce her novel to an audience already familiar with the author.
